chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Isma'il ibn Mihran from Hammad ibn 'Uthman said:

A severe shortage and famine struck the people of Medina, so much so that a wealthy man would mix wheat with barley and eat it, and as he spent the food, it was consumed. There was good food at the house of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) which he had purchased at the beginning of the year. He said to some of his freed slaves: 'Buy barley for us and mix it with this food, or sell it, for we dislike eating well while the people eat poor quality food.'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq demonstrate social equity during a famine?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) actively prevented 'al-hukrah' (hoarding for profit) by mixing his premium wheat with barley or selling it, ensuring his consumption mirrored the public's hardship rather than isolating him in luxury. This act exemplifies the Shia scholarly emphasis on social equity and the moral obligation of the wealthy to share in communal scarcity, distinguishing between mere storage and strategic hoarding. It highlights the principle that wealth should serve the community's well-being, preventing the disparity between the rich and the poor during crises.
